reason: I don't put a vendor with zero customers and no SOC 2 in the path of every customer trade, and I don't go first on anything. If Robinhood or Coinbase puts agent controls like this in front of their agents, I'll have it in next year's plan within two quarters, but today nobody I copy is doing it.
objection: An unaudited startup sitting inline between my customers' agents and execution is a new single point of failure my compliance team has to defend. On top of that, per-action overage pricing means I can't give finance a fixed number while I'm locking next year's budget, and the design-partner deal still asks me for a reference and a letter of intent naming a price before I know whether it works.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing Robinhood or Coinbase, or a broker my size, running it in production, plus a finished SOC 2 Type II and a flat annual price with no per-action overage.
